gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-ruda: Ruda reads tall and friendly on a screen, with a wire-thin skeleton and generous round lowercase. And Blockletter, the display face, is the one that gets to be precise and boxy, while Ruda does the quiet work of carrying the words.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-saira: Blockletter draws every stroke like a taut string, with a tall, squat-bellied midsection that looks pencil-sketched. Saira follows in plain sans, its rounded letters stretching high and its s left open enough to see through.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-sarpanch: Approachable is the first thing Sarpanch says, with a clearly open lowercase e and tight space under the ascenders. Sarpanch sits beneath Blockletter's straight-edged, constant strokes, so the heading feels ruled and the text feels softer.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-savate: Contemporary and tidy, Savate has a rounded o that nearly matches its capital. Reading on, its hairlines stay sturdy and its curves open wide, so lines of text move along with only a slight stroke modulation against Blockletter's ruler-drawn heading.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-schibsted-grot: Blockletter looks cut from strips of equal width, with a tall, squat-bellied midsection that feels sketched in pencil. Schibsted Grotesk follows in sans, its big open e and a keeping a long read easy.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-sen: Blockletter's squat, brush-pen belly sits in a tall midsection, drawn as if by a pencil that never presses harder. Sen follows with tall lowercase and constant-weight lines, and a long passage goes down smoothly because its curves stop before turning inward.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-sintony: Blockletter has no stroke modulation at all, just a tall squat-bellied midsection in pencil-sketch lines. And Sintony, a chunky plain sans with smooth curves, sits under it as the sturdier, easier voice on the page.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-sofia-sans: Blockletter's squat, brush-pen belly gives a tall midsection, all in pencil lines of one pressure. Sofia Sans takes over in plain sans, with tall lowercase like cut stencil pieces and rounded letters whose sides stay clearly open.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-sofia-sans-sem: Blockletter's tall midsection looks like a squat brush-pen belly, sketched by a pencil that never presses harder. And Sofia Sans Semi Condensed keeps a long passage moving, its lowercase nearly capital height with a visible entrance into every curve.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-sono: Flat, single-weight lines with a squat, tall-bellied middle. And Sono, a plain sans with tall lowercase and generous spacing, lets a long passage move along, each a with its mouth left ajar.
